stories.title: Trump touts Washington reflecting pool as US midterm battle reaches finale
summary: United States President Donald Trump devoted his final public remarks before Tuesday’s midterm elections to touting renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, even as Democrats sought to contain a rift in Michigan’s closely fought US Senate race.

A Democratic Senate could also block Trump’s lifetime appointments to the courts, including the Supreme Court. ‘Ransack, rape and plunder’ Trump warned Republican lawmakers in January that losing the midterms would lead to his impeachment.
Republicans have run a scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and branding Abdul El-Sayed, the Muslim Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, a terrorist.

stories.title: 'Over a million' abuse images found on phone of UK man who drugged, raped wife: prosecutor
summary: The court in Manchester, northwest England, is hearing the trial of nine men accused of various sexual offences against a woman who was abused by her husband — a man in his 60s who cannot be named to protect the victim’s identity.
The husband filmed and shared images of the abuse on the “internet and social media applications” with “other like-minded men”, prosecutor Louise Oakley told the court.
The husband pleaded guilty in September to some 60 sexual offences against his wife, including administering a substance with intent to stupefy or overpower her.

stories.title: At Kazakhstan forum, Pakistan presents Karachi and Gwadar ports as 'strategic gateways' for Central Asian trade
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan can serve as an important trade and transit corridor for the landlocked Central Asian countries, providing them with access to international maritime trade routes and global markets, Minister for Board of Investment (BoI) Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh said on Monday.
The minister invited regional and international investors to explore opportunities in key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, logistics, transportation, manufacturing and trade.

The minister emphasised that Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, youthful population, industrial capacity and seaport infrastructure positioned the country to play an important role in connecting Central Asian economies with international markets.

stories.title: PTI lawyer Salman Safdar says he met Imran, Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail
summary: PTI lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday said he met with party founder Imran Khan and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail, where they are both incarcerated.
When asked about Imran’s health, Akram replied that although health issues were discussed, the PTI would only speak about the legal cases.
Barrister Safdar’s last publicly reported meeting with Imran was held on April 8 this year, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting.

stories.title: Core inflation falls to 7.5% in Oct
summary: The non-energy and non-food inflation eased for the second consecutive month to 7.5% in October, putting a question mark over the central bank's assumption that increasing energy and food prices may "seep into core inflation", which was used to raise its policy rate.

Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) reported on Monday that the urban core inflation rate, calculated after excluding volatile energy and food prices, slowed down to 7.8% and rural inflation further fell to 7.1% in October.

"There is a risk that elevated food and energy inflation may further increase inflation expectations, which may seep into core inflation going forward," said the monetary policy statement issued by the central bank after the policy rate decision.

stories.title: Mineral incentive package on cards
summary: Furthermore, it is proposed that the withholding tax applicable to contractors and suppliers for mining projects may be reduced during the exploration and development phase and payment/deposit of such taxes may be deferred until the commencement of commercial production.
It has suggested that mining projects may be exempted from super tax for at least 30 years to improve project economics and maintain competitiveness with other mineral-producing jurisdictions.
Also, the withholding tax on dividends distributed by mining projects may be exempted for 15 years from commercial production.

stories.title: Pakistan's quiet resilience in first quarter of FY27
summary: The latest economic scorecard reflects steady policy under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government, close coordination with the military leadership under Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, and an economic team led by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb that kept reforms on course.

All three major rating agencies have upgraded Pakistan into the 'B' category with stable outlooks, rewarding the fiscal discipline and steady engagement with lenders central to Finance Minister Aurangzeb's approach.
And when fuel prices rose, a Rs75 billion relief scheme reached more than 12 million citizens who depend on motorcycles, rickshaws and small cars.

summary: "Pakistan needs financial innovation, and digital assets must complement the broader digital transformation," he said.

Pakistan established a statutory framework through the Virtual Assets Act 2026, assigning the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority responsibility for licensing and supervising virtual asset service providers.
He said restrictions on banks investing, trading or holding virtual assets through their own funds or customer deposits would remain.

stories.title: AI puts hourly billing model at risk
summary: According to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), software consultancy generated $364 million in export receipts during July to September FY27, while software exports contributed $157 million.
Firms must move up the software value chain by building specialised capability in enterprise AI integration, autonomous agentic workflows, data engineering and cybersecurity, he said.

The experts said Pakistan should also use its growing international engagement to promote locally developed technology products and services, helping domestic IT companies move beyond conventional outsourcing towards higher-value exports.

stories.title: Pakistan, China discuss regional and global developments in high-level meetings
summary: China’s Haixing appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to regional peace and stability and expressed confidence in further advancing the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries, according to the statement.

Haixing’s visit is “part of the ongoing high-level exchanges between Pakistan and China, reflecting the longstanding friendship and all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries”, FO had said earlier.
Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity.

stories.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns appointed new PIA chief executive officer
summary: The board of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Monday announced the appointment of Adrian Hamilton-Manns as its chief executive officer (CEO).

In a press release, PIA said Hamilton-Manns “brings a wealth of leadership and strategic experience within the global aviation sector”, adding that his appointment “marks a pivotal chapter” in the airline’s ongoing transformation.
A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for 75 per cent shares of PIA in December last year, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion.

stories.title: Fridge cyberattack hits supermarkets across Europe
summary: Major French retailers said on Oct 12 that hundreds of store refrigeration systems were hit by a cyberattack, which forced them to throw out spoiled food and raised concerns about food security.

According to Ica spokesperson Helena Johansson, the affected stores were all connected to an external refrigeration control system provided by Danish manufacturer Danfoss — the same supplier targeted in the Oct 12 cyberattack on French retailers.
Following the attack in France, Danfoss told AFP that most of the affected equipment were “legacy” products which “no longer receive software or security updates”.

stories.title: China calls for Middle East dialogue in talks with Iran, Saudi Arabia, Oman
summary: Beijing supports Tehran in “safeguarding its own sovereignty and security”, Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Ali Bagheri Kani, the deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, according to a Chinese statement.
China’s foreign ministry had not previously announced the visit by Bagheri Kani to Beijing.

Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia as part of “shuttle diplomacy visits… aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson told a news briefing.

stories.title: PM directs no leniency for banks slow in providing loans to farmers, SMEs
summary: Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif on Monday directed that no leniency should be shown to banks who were slow in providing loans to farmers, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and consumers under the Prime Minister’s Apna Ghar Scheme.
The scheme was launched by the prime minister in April, under which housing and construction loans of up Rs10 million were to be given on easy instalments.
The meeting was briefed that significant progress had been made by the SBP in providing loans on a priority basis to housing, agriculture, and SMEs.

stories.title: Political committee denies 'factionalism' within PTI, warns against violating party discipline
summary: The warning was issued by PTI’s political committee, which deliberated on party matters and the country’s overall situation.

According to a statement shared on X, the political committee clarified there “is no grouping or division in the party”. “The entire party is united with Imran Khan’s leadership, his ideology and his mission.

The committee also expressed “serious” reservations over the alleged arrests of party leaders and workers, particularly actions taken under MPO, and urged that no one be “targeted for revenge on the basis of political differences”.

stories.title: Pakistan Broadcasters Association elects new board directors, office-bearers
summary: The Pakistan Broadcasters Association (PBA) held its annual general body meeting on Friday to elect new members.
According to a press release, a majority of members from the TV and radio industry were present during the annual general body meeting in Karachi.
During the meeting, the general body elected three TV members as directors on the PBA board in the elected member category.

stories.title: Trump could launch nuclear strike on Iran within days, claims Tucker Carlson
summary: In a lengthy post on X, Carlson identified the potential target as Pickaxe Mountain, where Israeli intelligence allegedly believed Iran had resumed its nuclear enrichment program.
Under pressure from Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran.

Read: Trump says US will strike reported Iranian nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain 'very heavily' "Bibi (Netanyahu) calls Trump about it every day," Carlson quoted an unnamed informed observer as saying.

stories.title: Civilian convicted of offences against state cannot claim fundamental rights, govt says in report to LHC
summary: It accused him of concealing facts about his appeal, his father Hafeezullah Khan Niazi’s earlier proceedings, including a petition before the apex court and a contempt petition, as well as the anti-terrorism court’s May 25, 2023, order.
The report said Niazi had not annexed the military court’s order, an objection upheld by the high court in two other petitions.

The reply said that Niazi, held at Kot Lakhpat Jail, was convicted by a Field General Court Martial (FGCM) and sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment under Section 3 of the Official Secrets Act, 1923, read with Section 59 of the Army Act.

stories.title: Govt slashes petrol by Rs3.4, high-speed diesel by Rs7.76
summary: Earlier today, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

stories.title: Consumer inflation falls to 9.6pc in Oct from 10.3pc in Sept
summary: The slowdown in the inflation rate for the second consecutive month, measured by the Consumer Price Index, reversed the sharp increase recorded in August, when higher food and energy prices pushed the annual rate to 11.1pc from 9.2pc in July.
Food inflation dropped to 7.8pc in urban areas in October from 8.1pc in September.
The decline was much sharper in rural areas, where food inflation fell to 7.1pc from 7.7pc a month earlier.

stories.title: Pakistan fined for slow over-rate in tri-series final
summary: Pakistan have been fined five per cent of their match fees for maintaining a slow over-rate during their three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the One-day International tri-series final in Lahore on Saturday.

Pakistan had conceded 325-8 in the final before chasing down the target of 326 with three wickets and nine balls to spare, securing the tri-series title in front of their home crowd at Gaddafi Stadium.
His innings helped Pakistan recover from an early collapse and complete a joint-record successful chase in an ODI final.

stories.title: On eve of midterms, final polls point to Democratic gains, but can Republicans hold the Senate?
summary: Of the 100 seats in the Senate, Fox considers Democrats favoured in 48 Senate seats and Republicans in 45, with seven competitive states likely to determine control of the chamber.
Republicans believe that voters who supported him in those states could return to the polls and support Republican Senate candidates, even if the national political environment has shifted.

The network’s analysis presents two possible scenarios: a Democratic gain that could give the party as many as 55 Senate seats, or a Republican performance strong enough to preserve a majority of up to 52.

stories.title: 4 polio immunisation workers abducted in K-P’s Tank
summary: Four polio immunisation workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being fired upon in Khyber-Paktunkhwa’s Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Azam Warsak, were subsequently released.
According to details, the abduction incident in Tank occurred in a village located in the Sheikh Attar union council, where unidentified armed men abducted the four polio vaccination workers.
In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan.

stories.title: LHC directs jail authorities to arrange meeting between Noreen Niazi, her daughters
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Monday directed jail authorities to arrange a meeting between Noreen Niazi, the sister of PTI founder Imran Khan, and her two daughters on Tuesday (tomorrow).
Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the directives while hearing petitions challenging the extensions in the detention orders of Imran’s sisters Noreen, Uzma Khan and Aleema Khanum.
Aleema and Noreen, along with their sister Uzma Khan, were detained under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 in September, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

stories.title: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe
summary: A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and ​freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.
The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of ​cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses.

stories.title: Babar, Shaheen set for Quaid-e-Azam Trophy opening-round clash
summary: Abdullah Shafique will captain Sialkot Blues, while Mohammad Nawaz has been named skipper of Rawalpindi in the Silver tier.
Eight teams will compete in the Gold tier, with Karachi Blues, Faisalabad, Fata, Lahore Whites, Islamabad, Peshawar Blues, Multan and Sialkot Blues vying for the title.
In the Gold tier, Lahore Whites’ squad includes Babar, all-rounder Aamir Jamal, Tayyab Tahir and Noman Ali, while Fata will be led by Shaheen and also feature Khushdil Shah and Mohammad Wasim Khan.

stories.title: Shah Rukh Khan turns 61 as Bollywood stars celebrate the 'King' ahead of new film
summary: Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan marked his 61st birthday with a special treat for fans, unveiling Tu Mil Jaaye, the first song from his much-awaited film King, as birthday wishes poured in from family, friends and colleagues across the film industry.
Screengrab: suhanakhan2, theshilpashetty/Instagram Shah Rukh's daughter Suhana Khan took to Instagram to celebrate her father, sharing a picture of the poster of his upcoming film King.
Keeping her message short and sweet, she wrote, "Happy birthday king." Shilpa Shetty also shared a loving birthday tribute on her Instagram Story, calling Shah Rukh her forever Baazigar.

stories.title: Republicans, Democrats make midterm closing arguments as Michigan rift roils Senate race
summary: Over a fast-moving weekend, US Representative Haley Stevens, who lost the Michigan Democratic Senate primary to Abdul ‌El-Sayed in a bitter contest, suddenly switched to backing Republican Mike Rogers and appeared with him at a Detroit church.

Stevens' Sunday surprise came the same day a federal judge dismissed a US Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of election results in Alaska if Republican incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan narrowly loses in the battleground state.

"I've already been clear that that ad was not made by me, and I do not agree with the contents of that ad." When asked about Rep. Haley Stevens’ endorsement of Mike Rogers, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed said his focus is on the voters.

stories.title: Senior Communist Party official appreciates 'momentum' in Pakistan-China exchanges
summary: According to a statement issued by the PM Office, Haixing underscored the importance of continued high-level engagement and inter-party cooperation in further consolidating bilateral ties.

Mr. Liu Haixing, the Minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC) called on the Prime Minister Mr. Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad today.

He also appreciated the role of the IDCPC in promoting institutional linkages and cooperation between the political leadership of the two countries, while emphasising the importance of sustained political engagement and inter-party exchanges to bolster ties.

stories.title: Bangladesh garment workers protesting for higher wages clash with police
summary: Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs.
Garment workers gather to protest demanding higher minimum wages in Dhaka on November 2, 2026. — AFP Angry workers also set fire to a police vehicle.

The protests came despite the government’s announcement on Sunday that it would establish a wage board to review the minimum wage in the vital garment industry, which employs millions of people and generates the bulk of Bangladesh’s export earnings.

stories.title: Laden with eggs, robots race up sacred Chinese mountain
summary: Dozens of robots took on more than 3,000 steps up one of China’s most famous peaks on Monday, carrying eggs and watermelons in a race organisers billed as a test of real-world machine endurance, state media showed.
The fastest humanoid robot — belonging to Beijing-based team Zhishen Lingyue — completed a shorter race course in 27 minutes and 26 seconds.
The race, organised by the state-run China Media Group, featured cash prizes for winners in several categories, including the fastest robots and the best load-carrying four-legged machine.

stories.title: Junaid Khan calls for greater investment in independent music, diverse TV stories
summary: From the decline of dedicated music channels to the lack of male-centred narratives on television, Khan believes there is considerable room for the industry to diversify.

In a conversation with Atiqa Odho, Khan discussed his journey across music and acting, the emergence of independent musicians, the commercial priorities shaping television content and his aspirations to move into production.
Khan believes Pakistan's music industry has enormous potential, particularly with the emergence of younger artists and the accessibility of digital platforms.

stories.title: Islamabad court sentences man to 7-year jail term for filming objectionable video of teenage boy
summary: An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court sentenced Raja Haris Naveed to seven years of rigorous imprisonment in a cybercrime case involving the harassment of a 16-year-old boy and the recording of an objectionable video without his consent, it emerged on Monday.
Read: Two held for involvement in child abuse case In case of non-payment of the fine, the judge said the convict will have to serve an additional six months in prison.
In a similar case, an Islamabad court on October 22 sentenced two men to 10 years in prison each for blackmailing a 12-year-old girl and sharing her objectionable pictures.

stories.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns formally takes charge as PIA's new CEO
summary: Adrian Hamilton-Manns has formally assumed charge as the new chief executive officer (CEO) of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), bringing three decades of commercial aviation experience to the national flag carrier.
He brings a wealth of leadership & strategic experience, and his appointment marks a pivotal chapter in PIA’s ongoing transformation," the airline said in a statement posted on X on Monday.
PIA' Board is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Adrian Hamilton-Manns as the CEO.

stories.title: US midterms: Michigan Democrat's endorsement of Republican ruffles critical Senate race
summary: A prominent Michigan Democrat endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, giving President Donald Trump’s Republicans an unexpected boost in ​a critical US Senate race two days before midterm elections that will decide control of Congress.
He declined to directly address Stevens’ endorsement on Sunday. “This race was never about me,” El-Sayed told MS NOW. “It was never even about Mike Rogers.

stories.title: Oil refineries to bear Rs15b burden to ease fuel price pressure leading to Rs15 cut in petrol price
summary: The government on Monday announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Speaking about Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's approach to providing relief to consumers, Malik said the government was providing relief to the people according to its means.

Apart from the fuel relief scheme that was offering "targeted relief" to 13 million people, the government had undertaken several other measures to alleviate the burden on the masses, the petroleum minister stated.

stories.title: Pakistan assumes chairmanship of SCO Interbank Consortium for 2026-27
summary: Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) for 2026-27, the Ministry of Finance said on Monday.

The ministry congratulated Allana on assuming the responsibility and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening economic partnerships among SCO member states, facilitating cross-border trade and investment, and advancing regional integration and shared prosperity.
Pakistan hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Islamabad in October 2024 and is currently chairing the organisation’s Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure for 2025-26.

stories.title: Lahore's air quality index crosses 530 as pollution reaches hazardous levels
summary: Several other cities in Punjab also recorded extremely high pollution levels, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir.

Figure shows the top ranked polluted cities in Pakistan according to IQAir on Friday morning. — Screengrab via IQAir The worsening air quality comes amid a sharp increase in agricultural fire detections across Punjab.

Weather factor Meanwhile, a new analysis by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI) has questioned the extent of improvement in Lahore’s air quality during October, despite government claims that the city experienced its cleanest October in five years.

stories.title: AI models mostly smarter than top scientists, OpenAI's Altman says
summary: Advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models have progressed to become mostly smarter than the brightest scientists and capable of performing significant portions of white-collar work, OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said on Monday.
Altman stressed that despite the disruptive impact on global economies and employment, human judgement, creativity and accountability must remain central to the technology's deployment.

During the event, OpenAI announced partnerships with Emirati technology group G42 and state oil producer Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, marking the first global deployment of OpenAI's frontier models by an energy company.
